newsitem.title: USA: Three movies battle for top honors at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: Three movies battle for top honors at U.S. box office.

text.p: Three movies were tied for the No. 1 position at the weekend U.S. box office as studios tried to estimate how the Superbowl would affect theater attendance Sunday.

According to Exhibitor Relations, which collects the studios' data, reigning champion "Beverly Hills Ninja," "Jerry Maguire," and newcomer "In Love and War" each earned an estimated $5.9 million during the Friday-to-Sunday period.
The Eddie Murphy vehicle "Metro" slipped two notches to fourth in its second weekend with $5.6 million, and the musical "Evita" was also down two to fifth place and $5.5 million.

Two other movies made their debuts in the top 10 to rather disappointing results. "Fierce Creatures," starring the cast from the hit movie "A Fish Called Wanda," opened in eighth with $4.0 million. The 10th spot went to "Zeus and Roxanne," a children's movie, with $2.9 million.

Exhibitor Relations said the difficulty of estimating the extent to which people would stay home Sunday to watch the Superbowl football game on television rather than go to the movies meant that positions were certain to change when final data are released Monday.

"Jerry Maguire" and "Beverly Hills Ninja" are released by Sony Corp.. "In Love and War" is released by New Line Cinema, a unit of Time Warner Inc. "Metro" and "Evita" are released by Walt Disney Co. "Fierce Creatures" is released by Universal Pictures, a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd. . "Zeus and Roxanne" is released by MGM, which is owned by financier Kirk Kerkorian and Australia's Seven Network Ltd. .
